We define four vision-language tasks targeting different model capabilities.

we created a benchmark, Grounding Visual Illusion in Language (GVIL), which consists of four subtasks: Same-Difference Question Answering (SameDiffQA), Referential Question Answering (RefQA), Attribute Question Answering (AttrQA), and Referential Localization (RefLoc) to assess machines' alignment with the human under visual illusions.
outputs: The models generate answers to questions or predict bounding boxes based on visual illusions, which involves natural language generation in the form of responses to visual prompts.

We keep track of the Humanlike rate to measure the alignment between humans and VLMs, which is the percentage of examples where the machine gives exactly the same answers as humans.

We keep track of the Humanlike rate to measure the alignment between humans and VLMs, which is the percentage of examples where the machine gives exactly the same answers as humans. For the SameDiffQA task, we also compute the No-Illusion rate, which corresponds to the percentage of examples where the machine consistently considers the objects as the same under both illusion and illusion-free settings.
All the images and corresponding annotations are verified by at least three human annotators from our team.
guideline: The annotations include natural language questions, answers that humans would give under illusions, and bounding boxes for referring expressions formed under illusions. These were verified to ensure correctness and consistency with human perception.
